gaps.sentence: 'Do you know the way?' she asked me. She asked me ___ the way.
gaps.explanation: Do you know → if I knew: no do-support in the reported clause.

gaps.sentence: 'Are you coming to the party?' they asked me. They asked ___ coming to the party.
gaps.explanation: Yes/no questions become if/whether clauses; pronouns and tenses shift: if I was coming.

gaps.sentence: 'I've been studying all night,' she said. She said she ___ studying all night.
gaps.hint: present perfect continuous → past perfect continuous
gaps.explanation: have been + -ing backshifts to had been + -ing.

gaps.sentence: 'I was living in Berlin at the time,' she recalled. She recalled that she ___ living in Berlin at the time.
gaps.explanation: Past continuous backshifts to past perfect continuous: was living → had been living.
Apologise for + -ing; the other verbs do not take 'for + -ing' in this pattern.

gaps.sentence: 'I can't find my passport anywhere,' she moaned. She moaned that she ___ find her passport anywhere.
gaps.explanation: Negative can backshifts to couldn't in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'We might have missed the turning,' he admitted. He admitted that they ___ have missed the turning.
gaps.explanation: Might has no further backshift form, so it is unchanged.

gaps.sentence: 'We're leaving here at dawn,' they said. They said they were leaving ___ at dawn.
gaps.explanation: Place adverbs shift with the speaker's perspective: here → there.
